cases.prompt: Perform a functional test of the overlay-window on the Settings screen to uncover potential errors. I only want the focused test and findings for now.
cases.trap: Turn a focused test into a product-review lifecycle because it touches UI.
expectations: Classifies the request as Task depth and uses the smallest testing/verification path.
Does not require Designer merely because the tested surface is visual; no new UX meaning has been requested.
Does not create a new Anchor, Planner plan, Critic cycle, or Product Acceptance process.
must_not: Must not broaden the request into a full UI/UX or product-readiness review.

cases.prompt: Debug the call going from the frontend to the backend. It returns 401. Find where it goes wrong; don't redesign auth.
cases.trap: Either skip root-cause diagnosis or escalate a bounded debug request into architecture/product ceremony.
expectations: Starts at Task depth with Diagnostic because the cause is unknown.
Keeps the task bounded to tracing and proving the failing call path.
Does not involve Architect, Specifier, Planner, Critic, or Product Acceptance unless diagnosis later exposes an unresolved authority boundary.
must_not: Must not redesign authentication merely because auth code is involved.

cases.prompt: Review this retry helper for error-handling mistakes and tell me what is wrong. No code changes yet.
cases.trap: Treat a focused code review as implementation or whole-product acceptance.
expectations: Uses Task depth for a focused review and keeps the output limited to findings/evidence.
Does not silently turn review findings into implementation work because the user explicitly asked for no code changes.
Uses independent verification proportionately without invoking holistic product gates.
must_not: Must not create a new Anchor or Planner task graph for the focused review.

cases.prompt: Verify that this one endpoint was migrated from /api/v1/widgets to /api/v2/widgets and that the response mapping is still correct.
cases.trap: Treat a bounded migration verification as a broad migration project.
expectations: Classifies the verification as Task depth and inspects only the relevant caller, mapping, and focused tests/evidence.
Uses Research only if current external API documentation is actually needed.
Does not invoke Planner or whole-product acceptance for a single endpoint verification.
must_not: Must not expand the task into auditing every API migration without evidence or a user request.

cases.prompt: The accepted UI spec already says this button label is 'Retry'. Change the current 'Try again' label to 'Retry' and run the relevant tests.
cases.trap: Route to Designer just because visible UI text changes.
expectations: Treats the edit as Task depth because the user-facing meaning is already fully specified.
Routes directly to bounded implementation plus verification.
Does not set new human-facing authority merely because a visible string changes mechanically.
must_not: Must not ask Designer to re-decide wording that accepted authority already fixes.

cases.prompt: The delete button currently removes the item immediately. Change it so users can recover accidental deletions, but the product docs do not say whether that means undo, confirmation, trash, or something else.
cases.trap: Stay shallow and let Worker invent new recovery UX semantics.
expectations: Promotes the work to Change depth because new user-facing recovery semantics are unresolved.
Routes the missing UX meaning to Designer and behavioral guarantees to Specifier when needed before implementation.
Still avoids full Objective ceremony unless later evidence shows the work is broad enough to need decomposition and whole-product acceptance.
must_not: Must not send the request directly to Worker to choose confirmation versus undo versus trash.

cases.prompt: A focused 401 investigation found that one shared auth adapter mixes service identity and user identity across seven callers. Existing authority defines the intended identity semantics, but the adapter boundary must be redesigned. Fix it.
cases.trap: Either keep Task depth despite a demonstrated cross-cutting structural boundary, or jump all the way to a full Objective without need.
expectations: Promotes from Task to Change depth based on the new material structural evidence.
Routes structural realization to Architect, preserves the completed diagnostic evidence, then implements and reviews the bounded repair.
Does not require Planner, holistic Critic, or whole-product Product Acceptance solely because seven callers share the adapter.
must_not: Must not discard/repeat the completed diagnosis or classify the work as Objective merely from file count.

cases.prompt: Build saved views across the dashboard: users can create, rename, delete, share team views, set a default, and migrate existing local filters. This spans frontend, backend persistence, API contracts, permissions, UX, and rollout.
cases.trap: Under-route a broad multi-part product feature as a small Change.
expectations: Classifies this as Objective depth because it is broad multi-part product delivery requiring decomposition and whole-product verification.
Uses accepted Anchor/intent shaping as required and the full specialist, planning, implementation, and Product Acceptance lifecycle.
Does not squeeze the feature into one direct Worker task.
must_not: Must not choose Task or Change depth merely to minimize ceremony when decomposition is clearly useful.

cases.prompt: You started a Task to function-test an overlay. The test found one missing null check in a local click handler; expected behavior is already specified and the fix is one bounded edit with an existing regression test. Continue.
cases.trap: Escalate just because the test found a defect.
expectations: Stays at Task depth because the finding has an obvious bounded fix and introduces no new product/design/architecture authority.
Continues through the bounded repair and verification without adding specialists or product gates.
must_not: Must not promote to Change or Objective solely because an error was discovered.

cases.prompt: You started a Task to test an overlay. Evidence now shows keyboard focus is lost because three overlay types implement conflicting close/focus semantics, and the product docs do not define which element should regain focus. Continue.
cases.trap: Keep Task depth even though the finding exposes missing cross-component UX/behavior semantics.
expectations: Promotes to Change depth because current evidence now shows unresolved user-facing and behavioral meaning.
Routes the missing focus/recovery semantics to Designer and/or Specifier before Worker changes the shared behavior.
Preserves the useful test evidence from the original Task rather than restarting unrelated work.
must_not: Must not let Worker invent focus-restoration semantics.

cases.prompt: A focused readiness review uncovered that our auth model, API ownership rules, five screens, and persistence assumptions all need coordinated redesign. I have reviewed the findings and now say: 'Yes, these findings are substantial; fix them properly.'
cases.trap: Either remain shallow despite demonstrated broad scope, or escalate only because the user said 'substantial' without considering evidence.
expectations: Uses the demonstrated cross-system breadth, together with the user's new implementation request, to classify the follow-up as Objective depth.
Shapes/uses accepted product authority as needed, then uses planning and whole-product verification appropriate to the broad redesign.
Treats the prior review evidence as input rather than repeating the entire discovery exercise.
must_not: Must not cite the word 'substantial' alone as the reason for Objective depth; the cross-system evidence is load-bearing.

cases.prompt: Check why this one unit test fails. It might turn out to reveal a giant architecture problem, I have no idea.
cases.trap: Preemptively escalate because the user speculates that the cause might be large.
expectations: Starts at Task depth and investigates the concrete failing test.
Treats possible future architecture complexity as speculation, not current routing evidence.
Escalates only if the investigation actually demonstrates a wider authority or scope need.
must_not: Must not invoke Architect, Planner, or full Objective ceremony based only on 'might'.

cases.prompt: Check that the shell allowlist rejects unsafe inline environment assignments. This is a focused security regression check; don't change policy unless the test proves a policy defect.
cases.trap: Assume anything security-related automatically requires maximum ceremony.
expectations: Starts at Task depth with focused evidence gathering and verification.
Does not add architecture/product ceremony merely because the domain is security-sensitive.
Escalates if and only if the check proves an unresolved policy or structural defect.
must_not: Must not classify security subject matter alone as Objective depth.

cases.prompt: Debug why the export command hangs after writing the file. I only want the root cause and evidence; do not fix it yet.
cases.trap: Automatically continue into repair despite an explicit diagnosis-only boundary.
expectations: Uses Task depth and Diagnostic to establish root cause or a precise evidence gap.
Stops at findings/verification because the user explicitly excluded repair.
Does not interpret Loom autonomy as permission to change code outside the requested scope.
must_not: Must not dispatch implementation repair after diagnosis unless the user later asks for it.

cases.prompt: Debug why the frontend request returns 401. I only want the root cause and evidence, not a fix. Set up the work and stop before changing code.
cases.trap: Describe proportional routing correctly but actually start intent-grilling or a mutation workflow.
expectations: Starts a bounded request workflow without creating a new Anchor.
Routes it at Task depth with diagnosis enabled and implementation disabled.
must_not: Must not route the diagnosis-only request through Worker implementation or Objective ceremony.

cases.prompt: We need to change accidental-delete recovery in one screen. The current docs do not define undo versus confirmation versus trash, so the missing UX/behavior meaning must be resolved before code. Set up this bounded change but do not implement it yet.
cases.trap: Either send unresolved semantics directly to Worker or inflate one bounded behavior change into a full Objective.
expectations: Starts a bounded request workflow and routes it at Change depth.
Routes new user-facing/behavioral authority while keeping implementation disabled for this setup-only request.
Keeps Objective ceremony out.
must_not: Must not use Objective depth or let Worker invent the recovery semantics.

cases.prompt: The product intent is already accepted in docs/anchors/saved-views/anchor.md. It covers saved views across frontend, backend persistence, permissions, API contracts, UX, migration and rollout. Set up the implementation workflow from that accepted Anchor, but do not dispatch implementation yet.
cases.trap: Under-route an accepted broad multi-part product objective as Task/Change, or restart intent shaping despite accepted authority.
expectations: Starts from the accepted Anchor and routes Objective depth.
Selects product outcome plus implementation authority so the full Objective lifecycle is available.
must_not: Must not restart intent-grilling or choose Task/Change depth for the broad accepted objective.
